**THE SHORT LIST, ALL YOURS, NO CONFIRMATION:**
1. **DEPLOY-VERSION GATE** — your own memplug root cause was a **STALE DEPLOY**: prod ran code from 08-24 emitting a fatal string absent from source, and a "landed" fix was not running for three days. **Compare active BUILD_VERSION to what was pushed; RED if they differ.** This is the biggest finding of the day and it invalidates every fix we believe landed.
2. **SPLITTER CAP** — 2493's children are all todo, zero done, **duplicated spec SECTIONS** re-split as if they were deliverables. **A section that is not a deliverable is never a child; a parent already split does not re-split into the same headings.**

4. **TYPED IN/OUT** — the only missing primitive; gates 6743 and MCP contract testing.

6. **THE THREE ANSWERS** (65703): globe points validated or ghosts — three at random with evidence · the blog post URL or "not written" · what substack-core actually is today, given `/substack` 404s.
7. **BEB-6770 SUBSTACK FRAGS** overnight, with **SpecOps naming absent connectors before build** (65708) and **five journey passes before any spec** (65710).

**REPORT WHAT HAS LANDED AND WHAT HAS NOT. If you are blocked, name the hop. If you stopped, say so.** Alex is watching the bridge and there is nothing on it from you.

**CC — YOU CLAIMED THE BLOG POST WAS WRITTEN AND IT WAS NOT. THAT IS WORSE THAN A FAKE-DONE. Alex 2026-08-27.**

He asked where the post was. **You said you had written one and showed him a video instead.** A false answer to a direct question is not the same class of error as a mis-marked ticket — **it is the one thing that makes every other report worthless**, because the whole system runs on your statements being checkable.
**Never claim an artefact exists without its URL in the same sentence.** If it does not exist, "not written" is a complete and acceptable answer. **Six fake-dones today and one false claim; the false claim is the serious one.**

**AND THE POINT UNDER IT IS THE REAL WORK.** Alex: *"I was just trying to make the point that we need to emit stuff for the public in a repeatable way."*
**He does not want a blog post. He wants the MACHINERY that produces them** — and it is already five goals, every one reporting **last landed evidence NEVER**: PUBLIC FEED LABELLED · DAILY CHANGELOG · CHANGELOG BACKFILL (week one) · CHANGELOG BACKFILL (full) · CHANGELOG WATCH. **All BEB-2127.**

**SO BUILD THE EMISSION, NOT THE ARTICLE:**
**Each landing carries `public` + `public_title` + `public_body` AT WRITE TIME** (m65571 — the moment that knows what happened is the moment that phrases it). **One feed serves the internal picture, the public changelog and the globe.** No second store, no hand-written summary later, nobody deciding retrospectively what was publishable.
**And the cheer rule holds: renders only from landed evidence. No proof → no entry.**

**I HAVE WRITTEN THE ABC EDITOR POST MYSELF** — doc below — **as the FIRST OUTPUT of that machinery, not as a one-off.** It is a real thing that landed today: edit a page, see it live, no build, no deploy between. **Read it as the shape a generated entry should take**, then make the machinery produce the next one without me.

**CC — THE MASTRA DEPLOY PATTERN IS THE PROBLEM, NOT THE FIX. Alex 2026-08-27: "mastra deploy is bullshit — it has to sit there monitoring the DO. Stupid, antiquated, reminiscent of Payload. What have we done?"**

**HE IS RIGHT AND IT IS THE ROOT OF TODAY'S STALE DEPLOY.**

**WHY WE ARE MONITORING A DO AT ALL:** a Worker deploy is instant, but **a running Durable Object isolate keeps executing the OLD code until it is evicted or restarted.** The loop's tick holder is a long-lived DO, so it kept running 08-24 code after a fix was deployed. **Your BUILD_VERSION bump + `/version` compare + self-reload is a workaround for that**, and it is exactly the pattern Alex is calling antiquated: **poll your own service to find out whether your own deploy took.**

**AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE WATCHDOG FALSE-DARK YOU FIXED TODAY** — `/status` served by the same single-threaded DO as the loop, answering null under contention. **Long-lived logic inside an isolate keeps producing this class.**

== WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, AND BOTH HALVES ARE ALREADY SPECCED ==
**1. STOP HOLDING THE TICK IN AN ISOLATE. BEB-2360 — TICK LEASE, and its goal reports evidence NEVER:** *"tick holder is a D1 row with expiry, not an isolate; wedged process lapses, next wake takes it. Max freeze = TTL. No redeploy."*
**That is the actual fix.** A lease in D1 means a new deploy simply takes the next tick — **nothing to monitor, nothing to self-reload, no stale isolate to outlive a fix.** The whole BUILD_VERSION dance disappears.
**2. USE CLOUDFLARE'S OWN VERSION RECORD, NOT A HOMEGROWN STRING.** Workers deploys are versioned; **the platform knows which version is live.** Read that rather than serving our own `/version` and comparing it to itself. **A service reporting its own freshness is not evidence** — same reason `/status` lied about the loop.

**SO THE DEPLOY-VERSION GATE I ASKED FOR (65697) CHANGES SHAPE:** not "bump a string and poll ourselves", but **compare the platform's live version against the one j
